etteilla-01.name: Le Chaos (The Questioner - Male)
etteilla-01.Scene: Le Chaos shows a male figure — the Questioner — surrounded by swirling primordial forms. In the Livre de Thot, this first card represents the male querent who is asking the oracle, and its chaotic surround evokes the undifferentiated void before creation. Etteilla placed this card first to acknowledge the questioner's presence as the starting point of any reading, the self in the middle of what is unknown.

etteilla-02.name: La Lumière (Light/Enlightenment)
etteilla-02.Scene: La Lumière shows the first emanation of divine light — rays of brightness parting from darkness. This is Etteilla's version of the first day of creation: the separation of light from chaos, the initial act of divine intelligence making the formless into something perceptible. In the Livre de Thot, the image is celestial and expansive, the rays emanating outward as the primordial act of enlightenment.

etteilla-03.name: Les Plantes (Plants/Growth)
etteilla-03.Scene: Les Plantes depicts the emergence of vegetation from the earth — the second day of Etteilla's Genesis sequence, when plant life covers the ground with green. The image shows leaves, trees, or botanical forms emerging as the world's creative fertility first manifests. Etteilla associated this card with growth, patience, and the fecundity of the natural world.

etteilla-04.name: Le Ciel (The Heavens)
etteilla-04.Scene: Le Ciel depicts the celestial vault — the heavens as a dome or expanse above the earth. This card represents the firmament of creation, the separation of above and below that structures the world. In the Etteilla system the celestial card is associated with aspiration, vision, and the realm of ideals that exists above the material plane.

etteilla-05.name: L'Homme et les Quadrupèdes (Man and Quadrupeds)
etteilla-05.Scene: L'Homme et les Quadrupèdes shows the human figure alongside four-legged animals in the scene of creation. Man and beast together on the earth — the fifth day of Etteilla's sequence — represents the world populated with its creatures, the human standing among and over the animal kingdom. The card is associated with the earthly partnership between human intelligence and animal nature.

etteilla-06.name: Les Astres (The Celestial Bodies)
etteilla-06.Scene: Les Astres shows the arrangement of celestial bodies — sun, moon, and stars placed in their positions in the firmament. This card represents the ordering of the heavens, the celestial mechanics that govern time and season. In the Livre de Thot, the celestial bodies are depicted as luminous forms in a starry vault, each in its proper place in the cosmic order.

etteilla-07.name: Les Oiseaux et les Poissons (Birds and Fishes)
etteilla-07.Scene: Les Oiseaux et les Poissons shows birds in the air and fish in the water — the creatures of the in-between realms, neither fully earthly nor fully celestial. In Etteilla's Genesis sequence this card represents the animation of the atmosphere and the deep waters with life. Birds occupy the middle air and fish the dark below, together completing the spectrum of created life.

etteilla-08.name: Le Repos (Rest)
etteilla-08.Scene: Le Repos depicts a figure or scene of rest — the Sabbath day after the completion of creation. In Etteilla's system this card is not merely cessation but sacred rest, the divine pause that consecrates what has been made. The image in the Livre de Thot shows a figure in repose, the creative work completed and the world given over to a period of contemplation and rest.

etteilla-09.name: La Justice (Justice)
etteilla-09.Scene: La Justice appears as the fourth cardinal virtue in the Etteilla sequence, depicted as a crowned or robed female figure with sword and scales. Etteilla placed Justice at position nine rather than at the Marseille position, incorporating the virtue into his revised allegorical sequence. The image follows the classical iconography of Justice as the weigher of deeds.

etteilla-10.name: La Tempérance (Temperance)
etteilla-10.Scene: La Tempérance appears as the cardinal virtue of moderation at position ten, typically depicted as a female figure pouring liquid between two vessels. Etteilla's Tempérance follows the conventional allegorical personification of this virtue, the measured exchange between two containers representing balance and self-regulation.

etteilla-11.name: La Force (Strength)
etteilla-11.Scene: La Force appears at position eleven as the virtue of fortitude — a figure subduing a lion or overcoming a physical challenge through courage and patient strength. Etteilla's Force follows the traditional personification of this virtue, the human mastery of instinct expressed as gentle physical dominance.

etteilla-12.name: La Prudence (Prudence)
etteilla-12.Scene: La Prudence represents the fourth classical virtue at position twelve in the Etteilla sequence — the virtue of wisdom and foresight, associated with the mirror (self-knowledge) and the serpent (wisdom). Etteilla's inclusion of Prudence as a separate card is one of his major departures from the Marseille tradition, which lacks Prudence among its four virtues.

etteilla-13.name: Le Grand Prêtre (The High Priest)
etteilla-13.Scene: Le Grand Prêtre (The High Priest) represents Etteilla's equivalent of the Hierophant or Pope — an enthroned spiritual authority with sacred vestments and sceptre, presiding over a scene of religious instruction or blessing. The title 'Grand Prêtre' emphasizes priestly rather than papal authority, the intermediary between divine and human realms.

etteilla-14.name: Le Diable (The Devil)
etteilla-14.Scene: Le Diable appears at position fourteen in the Etteilla system as the figure of infernal temptation and bondage — typically depicted with horns and wings, a pedestal with bound or chained figures below. Etteilla's Devil card follows the conventional allegorical type while placing it earlier in his renumbered sequence than in Marseille tradition.

etteilla-15.name: Le Magicien ou le Bateleur (The Magician/Juggler)
etteilla-15.Scene: Le Magicien ou le Bateleur appears at position fifteen in the Etteilla system, the conjurer or Magician equivalent. In the Etteilla sequence the Magician appears late among the allegorical cards rather than first, his skill and mastery positioned as mature achievement rather than initial promise. The image shows a figure at a table with the tools of his art.

etteilla-16.name: Le Jugement Dernier (The Last Judgment)
etteilla-16.Scene: Le Jugement Dernier (The Last Judgment) shows the divine angel with trumpet summoning the risen dead — a conventional allegorical rendering of the Christian eschatological scene. In Etteilla's system the Judgment appears at position sixteen, integrated into the revised allegorical sequence between the Magician and Death.

etteilla-17.name: La Mort (Death)
etteilla-17.Scene: La Mort shows the skeleton with scythe harvesting the field of the living. Death appears at position seventeen in the Etteilla sequence, the conventional allegorical figure of mortality positioned mid-sequence. The image follows the standard European iconography of Death as the universal harvester.

etteilla-18.name: Le Capucin (The Hermit/Monk)
etteilla-18.Scene: Le Capucin (The Friar/Hermit) shows a monk or Capuchin friar in a cowl and habit, a figure of religious withdrawal and contemplation. Etteilla renamed the Hermit as a Capucin, giving the card a more specifically French monastic character — the Capuchin order being a visible presence in 18th-century French religious life. The figure holds a lantern or staff.

etteilla-19.name: Le Temple Foudroyé (The Struck Temple)
etteilla-19.Scene: Le Temple Foudroyé (The Struck Temple) shows a classical or Egyptian temple or column struck by lightning, with figures falling. Etteilla's version of the Tower card refers specifically to a temple rather than a tower, evoking the destruction of sacred architecture — perhaps resonating with the French Enlightenment's complicated relationship to the Church and its institutions.

etteilla-20.name: La Roue de Fortune (Wheel of Fortune)
etteilla-20.Scene: La Roue de Fortune shows the conventional spinning wheel of Fortune with ascending and descending figures. At position twenty in the Etteilla sequence, the Wheel is positioned late in the allegorical series, Fortune's arbitrariness placed in a context already structured by the virtues and the allegorical narrative.

etteilla-21.name: Le Despote Africain (African Despot/King)
etteilla-21.Scene: Le Despote Africain (The African Despot) is Etteilla's most remarkable and culturally specific trump — a crowned African or dark-complexioned ruler who replaces the World card at the apex of the allegorical sequence. This card has been identified as reflecting 18th-century French orientalism and the deck's claimed Egyptian origins, placing an exotic sovereign at the summit of the ordering sequence.

etteilla-22.name: Roi de Bâton (King of Wands)
etteilla-22.Scene: Roi de Bâton (King of Wands) shows a crowned or enthroned male figure associated with the wand suit — a king who embodies the fiery, creative, and enterprising qualities of the baton. In the Etteilla system the King of Wands is associated with creative authority and entrepreneurial leadership, a figure who commands through vision and enthusiasm.

etteilla-23.name: Reine de Bâton (Queen of Wands)
etteilla-23.Scene: Reine de Bâton (Queen of Wands) shows a crowned female figure associated with the wand suit — a queen of warmth, creativity, and passionate generosity. In the Etteilla system the Queen of Wands embodies the feminine expression of the suit's fire: nurturing creativity, enthusiastic support of others, and the warmth that sustains creative endeavors.

etteilla-24.name: Chevalier de Bâton (Knight of Wands)
etteilla-24.Scene: Chevalier de Bâton (Knight of Wands) shows a mounted figure in action, the wand suit's knight carrying the suit's fiery energy into active pursuit. In the Etteilla system the Knight of Wands is the messenger or pursuer of creative enterprise — swift, enthusiastic, and perhaps impetuous in the pursuit of what fires him.

etteilla-25.name: Valet de Bâton (Page of Wands)
etteilla-25.Scene: Valet de Bâton (Page of Wands) shows a youthful standing figure with the wand as his attribute — the suit's page or messenger, a young person of creative curiosity and eager enthusiasm. In the Etteilla system the Page of Wands brings news of creative ventures and embodies the beginner's energy of open, exploratory enthusiasm.

etteilla-26.name: Dix de Bâton (Ten of Wands)
etteilla-26.Scene: Dix de Bâton (Ten of Wands) shows ten wand pip symbols in the Etteilla convention — ten batons arranged in the card's field, often with keywords for their divinatory meanings printed in the borders. The ten of wands in the Etteilla system is associated with overload and burden, the weight of accumulated creative obligation.

etteilla-27.name: Neuf de Bâton (Nine of Wands)
etteilla-27.Scene: Neuf de Bâton (Nine of Wands) shows nine wand pip symbols with associated divinatory keywords. The nine of wands in the Etteilla system is associated with resilience and defensive strength — the prepared position of one who has faced many challenges and stands ready for the next.

etteilla-28.name: Huit de Bâton (Eight of Wands)
etteilla-28.Scene: Huit de Bâton (Eight of Wands) shows eight wand pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The eight of wands in the Etteilla system is associated with swift communication and rapid movement — the velocity of messages and events in flight.

etteilla-29.name: Sept de Bâton (Seven of Wands)
etteilla-29.Scene: Sept de Bâton (Seven of Wands) shows seven wand pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The seven of wands in the Etteilla system is associated with courage in the face of opposition — standing one's ground against multiple challengers.

etteilla-30.name: Six de Bâton (Six of Wands)
etteilla-30.Scene: Six de Bâton (Six of Wands) shows six wand pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The six of wands in the Etteilla system is associated with victory and public recognition — the triumphant return after a creative achievement.

etteilla-31.name: Cinq de Bâton (Five of Wands)
etteilla-31.Scene: Cinq de Bâton (Five of Wands) shows five wand pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The five of wands in the Etteilla system is associated with conflict and competition — the contest of multiple creative energies in active opposition.

etteilla-32.name: Quatre de Bâton (Four of Wands)
etteilla-32.Scene: Quatre de Bâton (Four of Wands) shows four wand pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The four of wands in the Etteilla system is associated with celebration and homecoming — the stable structure of achieved creative success, a foundation for festivity.

etteilla-33.name: Trois de Bâton (Three of Wands)
etteilla-33.Scene: Trois de Bâton (Three of Wands) shows three wand pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The three of wands in the Etteilla system is associated with foresight and enterprise — the visionary look toward the horizon, creative momentum directed outward.

etteilla-34.name: Deux de Bâton (Two of Wands)
etteilla-34.Scene: Deux de Bâton (Two of Wands) shows two wand pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The two of wands in the Etteilla system is associated with choice and personal power — the individual who holds the world in their hands, the creative will at a point of decision.

etteilla-35.name: As de Bâton (Ace of Wands)
etteilla-35.Scene: As de Bâton (Ace of Wands) shows a single wand pip as the suit's foundational emblem. In the Etteilla system the Ace of Wands is the concentrated essence of the suit's creative fire — the seed of enterprise, the initial spark of creative impulse before it divides into specific projects.

etteilla-36.name: Roi de Coupe (King of Cups)
etteilla-36.Scene: Roi de Coupe (King of Cups) shows a crowned or enthroned male figure associated with the cup suit — a king who embodies emotional maturity, wisdom in feeling, and the patient governance of the inner life. In the Etteilla system the King of Cups is a figure of professional and emotional authority, one who balances intellect and feeling.

etteilla-37.name: Reine de Coupe (Queen of Cups)
etteilla-37.Scene: Reine de Coupe (Queen of Cups) shows a crowned female figure associated with the cup suit — a queen of emotional intelligence, intuition, and compassionate understanding. In the Etteilla system the Queen of Cups embodies the feminine expression of the suit's water: deep feeling, creative imagination, and the capacity to understand others through empathy.

etteilla-38.name: Chevalier de Coupe (Knight of Cups)
etteilla-38.Scene: Chevalier de Coupe (Knight of Cups) shows a mounted figure bearing a cup — the suit's active messenger of emotional and romantic quests. In the Etteilla system the Knight of Cups arrives with an emotional invitation or romantic proposal, a figure who carries the suit's feeling forward on the wings of imagination.

etteilla-39.name: Valet de Coupe (Page of Cups)
etteilla-39.Scene: Valet de Coupe (Page of Cups) shows a youthful figure with the cup as attribute — a sensitive young person of imaginative and artistic inclinations. In the Etteilla system the Page of Cups brings messages of an emotional or creative nature, a young person attuned to the inner world and receptive to feeling.

etteilla-40.name: Dix de Coupe (Ten of Cups)
etteilla-40.Scene: Dix de Coupe (Ten of Cups) shows ten cup pip symbols with divinatory keywords. In the Etteilla system the ten of cups is associated with lasting happiness and family harmony — the emotional suit at its most fulfilled and domestic.

etteilla-41.name: Neuf de Coupe (Nine of Cups)
etteilla-41.Scene: Neuf de Coupe (Nine of Cups) shows nine cup pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The nine of cups in the Etteilla system is associated with wishes fulfilled and satisfaction — the contented state of one whose emotional desires have been met.

etteilla-42.name: Huit de Coupe (Eight of Cups)
etteilla-42.Scene: Huit de Coupe (Eight of Cups) shows eight cup pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The eight of cups in the Etteilla system is associated with leaving behind what has been outgrown — the emotional departure from situations or relationships that no longer sustain.

etteilla-43.name: Sept de Coupe (Seven of Cups)
etteilla-43.Scene: Sept de Coupe (Seven of Cups) shows seven cup pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The seven of cups in the Etteilla system is associated with fantasy, illusion, and the proliferation of choices in the emotional domain — too many cups, too many desires, imagination run to excess.

etteilla-44.name: Six de Coupe (Six of Cups)
etteilla-44.Scene: Six de Coupe (Six of Cups) shows six cup pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The six of cups in the Etteilla system is associated with nostalgia, past happiness, and the emotional memories of earlier times — the cups as containers of what has been felt before.

etteilla-45.name: Cinq de Coupe (Five of Cups)
etteilla-45.Scene: Cinq de Coupe (Five of Cups) shows five cup pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The five of cups in the Etteilla system is associated with loss and disappointment — what has spilled from the emotional containers, the focus on what is gone rather than what remains.

etteilla-46.name: Quatre de Coupe (Four of Cups)
etteilla-46.Scene: Quatre de Coupe (Four of Cups) shows four cup pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The four of cups in the Etteilla system is associated with contemplation and emotional saturation — a stable arrangement that has become too enclosed, feeling held in a structure that limits further growth.

etteilla-47.name: Trois de Coupe (Three of Cups)
etteilla-47.Scene: Trois de Coupe (Three of Cups) shows three cup pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The three of cups in the Etteilla system is associated with celebration and abundance — three cups raised in community, emotional joy shared among companions.

etteilla-48.name: Deux de Coupe (Two of Cups)
etteilla-48.Scene: Deux de Coupe (Two of Cups) shows two cup pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The two of cups in the Etteilla system is associated with partnership and emotional union — two cups meeting, the primal dyad of emotional exchange and mutual recognition.

etteilla-49.name: As de Coupe (Ace of Cups)
etteilla-49.Scene: As de Coupe (Ace of Cups) shows a single cup as the suit's foundational emblem, often depicted as an ornate chalice. In the Etteilla system the Ace of Cups is the undivided potential of emotional life — the vessel before it is filled or emptied, receptivity in its most concentrated and generative form.

etteilla-50.name: Roi d'Épée (King of Swords)
etteilla-50.Scene: Roi d'Épée (King of Swords) shows a crowned or enthroned male figure with the sword as his attribute — a king of intellectual authority, sharp judgment, and the clear articulation of truth. In the Etteilla system the King of Swords is a figure of professional authority in law, medicine, or intellectual life, one who wields the blade of discernment.

etteilla-51.name: Reine d'Épée (Queen of Swords)
etteilla-51.Scene: Reine d'Épée (Queen of Swords) shows a crowned female figure with the sword — a queen of keen perception, clear communication, and the independence of mind. In the Etteilla system the Queen of Swords is a figure who has experienced loss and developed wisdom through it, her clarity a product of emotional experience rather than innocence.

etteilla-52.name: Chevalier d'Épée (Knight of Swords)
etteilla-52.Scene: Chevalier d'Épée (Knight of Swords) shows a mounted figure charging with sword raised — the suit's active rank carrying discernment and decisive action into swift motion. The Knight of Swords in the Etteilla system is the most direct and sometimes impetuous expression of the suit's cutting intelligence.

etteilla-53.name: Valet d'Épée (Page of Swords)
etteilla-53.Scene: Valet d'Épée (Page of Swords) shows a youthful standing figure with sword — the suit's youngest court rank, a curious and alert young person who gathers information and maintains a careful watch. The Page of Swords in the Etteilla system is the vigilant observer, the spy or investigator in a youthful guise.

etteilla-54.name: Dix d'Épée (Ten of Swords)
etteilla-54.Scene: Dix d'Épée (Ten of Swords) shows ten sword pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The ten of swords in the Etteilla system is associated with ruin and painful conclusion — the maximum accumulation of the suit's cutting force resulting in the final severance.

etteilla-55.name: Neuf d'Épée (Nine of Swords)
etteilla-55.Scene: Neuf d'Épée (Nine of Swords) shows nine sword pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The nine of swords in the Etteilla system is associated with anxiety, nightmares, and mental suffering — the suit's mental energy turned against itself in a spiral of fearful thought.

etteilla-56.name: Huit d'Épée (Eight of Swords)
etteilla-56.Scene: Huit d'Épée (Eight of Swords) shows eight sword pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The eight of swords in the Etteilla system is associated with restriction and confusion — the binding of the mind by its own constructions, the feeling of being trapped by thought.

etteilla-57.name: Sept d'Épée (Seven of Swords)
etteilla-57.Scene: Sept d'Épée (Seven of Swords) shows seven sword pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The seven of swords in the Etteilla system is associated with strategy, theft, or the evasive maneuver — the suit's intelligence applied to circumventing opposition rather than confronting it directly.

etteilla-58.name: Six d'Épée (Six of Swords)
etteilla-58.Scene: Six d'Épée (Six of Swords) shows six sword pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The six of swords in the Etteilla system is associated with transition and passage — moving away from turbulent waters toward calmer conditions, the journey of recovery from mental turmoil.

etteilla-59.name: Cinq d'Épée (Five of Swords)
etteilla-59.Scene: Cinq d'Épée (Five of Swords) shows five sword pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The five of swords in the Etteilla system is associated with defeat and hollow victory — the pyrrhic win that comes at too great a cost, conflict that damages all parties.

etteilla-60.name: Quatre d'Épée (Four of Swords)
etteilla-60.Scene: Quatre d'Épée (Four of Swords) shows four sword pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The four of swords in the Etteilla system is associated with rest and recuperation — the knight's effigy on a tomb, rest as preparation for renewed action after a period of mental or physical exhaustion.

etteilla-61.name: Trois d'Épée (Three of Swords)
etteilla-61.Scene: Trois d'Épée (Three of Swords) shows three sword pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The three of swords in the Etteilla system is associated with heartbreak and sorrow — the precise moment of loss or separation that leaves a wound in the emotional life.

etteilla-62.name: Deux d'Épée (Two of Swords)
etteilla-62.Scene: Deux d'Épée (Two of Swords) shows two sword pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The two of swords in the Etteilla system is associated with stalemate and willful blindness — two blades crossed in a truce that is actually an avoidance of the truth.

etteilla-63.name: As d'Épée (Ace of Swords)
etteilla-63.Scene: As d'Épée (Ace of Swords) shows a single sword as the suit's foundational emblem. In the Etteilla system the Ace of Swords is the undivided force of mental clarity — the blade of truth before it is used for either justice or cruelty, the intellectual potential in its most concentrated form.

etteilla-64.name: Roi de Denier (King of Coins)
etteilla-64.Scene: Roi de Denier (King of Coins) shows a crowned or enthroned male figure associated with the coin suit — a king of practical authority, material success, and the stable governance of earthly resources. In the Etteilla system the King of Coins is a figure of financial and material authority, one who commands through demonstrated competence and reliable prosperity.

etteilla-65.name: Reine de Denier (Queen of Coins)
etteilla-65.Scene: Reine de Denier (Queen of Coins) shows a crowned female figure associated with the coin suit — a queen of practical nurturing, material generosity, and the intelligent management of earthly resources. In the Etteilla system the Queen of Coins is a figure of domestic authority and material warmth, one who makes the household flourish through careful stewardship.

etteilla-66.name: Chevalier de Denier (Knight of Coins)
etteilla-66.Scene: Chevalier de Denier (Knight of Coins) shows a mounted figure bearing a coin — the suit's active rank carrying material ambition into patient, methodical pursuit. The Knight of Coins in the Etteilla system is the most deliberate and careful of the suit's court figures, his progress slow but reliable.

etteilla-67.name: Valet de Denier (Page of Coins)
etteilla-67.Scene: Valet de Denier (Page of Coins) shows a youthful figure studying a coin — the suit's youngest court rank, a diligent student of practical matters and material skills. The Page of Coins in the Etteilla system is the earnest learner of practical competencies, a young person focused on developing real-world skills.

etteilla-68.name: Dix de Denier (Ten of Coins)
etteilla-68.Scene: Dix de Denier (Ten of Coins) shows ten coin pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The ten of coins in the Etteilla system is associated with material completion and generational wealth — the abundance that extends beyond the individual to the family and community.

etteilla-69.name: Neuf de Denier (Nine of Coins)
etteilla-69.Scene: Neuf de Denier (Nine of Coins) shows nine coin pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The nine of coins in the Etteilla system is associated with material comfort and refined self-sufficiency — the enjoyment of earned prosperity in a cultivated environment.

etteilla-70.name: Huit de Denier (Eight of Coins)
etteilla-70.Scene: Huit de Denier (Eight of Coins) shows eight coin pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The eight of coins in the Etteilla system is associated with skill development and craftsmanship — the diligent repetitive practice that builds material competence.

etteilla-71.name: Sept de Denier (Seven of Coins)
etteilla-71.Scene: Sept de Denier (Seven of Coins) shows seven coin pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The seven of coins in the Etteilla system is associated with patient waiting for material results — the farmer who has planted and now waits to harvest, the assessment of what has been invested.

etteilla-72.name: Six de Denier (Six of Coins)
etteilla-72.Scene: Six de Denier (Six of Coins) shows six coin pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The six of coins in the Etteilla system is associated with generosity and equitable distribution — the giving and receiving of material resources in balanced exchange.

etteilla-73.name: Cinq de Denier (Five of Coins)
etteilla-73.Scene: Cinq de Denier (Five of Coins) shows five coin pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The five of coins in the Etteilla system is associated with material hardship and exclusion — the experience of being cold and without support, material or spiritual poverty.

etteilla-74.name: Quatre de Denier (Four of Coins)
etteilla-74.Scene: Quatre de Denier (Four of Coins) shows four coin pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The four of coins in the Etteilla system is associated with material security and possessiveness — the stable holding of resources that risks becoming rigid attachment.

etteilla-75.name: Trois de Denier (Three of Coins)
etteilla-75.Scene: Trois de Denier (Three of Coins) shows three coin pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The three of coins in the Etteilla system is associated with skilled work and collaborative achievement — the master craftsman at work, material competence applied in a context of recognized expertise.

etteilla-76.name: Deux de Denier (Two of Coins)
etteilla-76.Scene: Deux de Denier (Two of Coins) shows two coin pip symbols with divinatory keywords. The two of coins in the Etteilla system is associated with balance and juggling — the management of multiple material responsibilities simultaneously, adaptability in the face of fluctuating circumstances.

etteilla-77.name: As de Denier (Ace of Coins)
etteilla-77.Scene: As de Denier (Ace of Coins) shows a single coin as the suit's foundational emblem. In the Etteilla system the Ace of Coins is the undivided potential of material manifestation — the seed of prosperity, the opportunity for practical achievement in its most concentrated form.

etteilla-78.name: La Folie (The Fool)
etteilla-78.Scene: La Folie (The Fool) is Etteilla's version of the unnumbered Fool, placed at card 78 — the deck's last card number — rather than at the beginning or end of the trump sequence. The Fool appears as a conventionally wandering or comic figure, but Etteilla's placement of the Folie at 78 reflects his systematic renumbering of the entire tarot.

kw-balance.name: Balance
kw-balance.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with the divinatory theme of Balance in the Etteilla system — the quality of equilibrium between opposing forces, the measure of just proportion. Balance in the Etteilla tradition is associated with the Cardinal Virtue of Justice, with the two-cup Temperance, and with pip cards in the middle range of the suits.

kw-creativity.name: Creativity
kw-creativity.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with Creativity in the Etteilla system — the generative impulse, the power of imaginative invention and artistic expression. Creativity in the Etteilla tradition is associated with the Wands suit and with the early Genesis cards' depiction of the creative acts of divine order.

kw-truth.name: Truth
kw-truth.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with Truth in the Etteilla system — the quality of accurate perception and honest expression. Truth in the Etteilla tradition is associated with the Cardinal Virtues, with the Swords suit's cutting clarity, and with the oracle's fundamental purpose of revealing what is actually the case.

kw-patience.name: Patience
kw-patience.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with Patience in the Etteilla system — the quality of waiting, enduring, and allowing things to unfold in their proper time. Patience in the Etteilla tradition is associated with the slower Coin suit cards and with the Genesis sequence's depiction of creation as an ordered temporal process.

kw-security.name: Security
kw-security.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with Security in the Etteilla system — the quality of stable foundation, material safety, and protection from threat. Security in the Etteilla tradition is associated with stable pip cards in the Coin suit and with figures of established authority.

kw-wisdom.name: Wisdom
kw-wisdom.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with Wisdom in the Etteilla system — deep understanding, the knowledge that comes from experience rather than from mere information. Wisdom in the Etteilla tradition is associated with the Prudence trump, with senior court figures, and with the accumulated insight of the oracle itself.

kw-abundance.name: Abundance
kw-abundance.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with Abundance in the Etteilla system — the fullness of material, emotional, or creative resources. Abundance in the Etteilla tradition is associated with the ten-pip cards and the higher pip counts in each suit.

kw-clarity.name: Clarity
kw-clarity.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with Clarity in the Etteilla system — the quality of clear perception, unobstructed understanding, and the removal of confusion or illusion. Clarity in the Etteilla tradition is associated with the Swords suit's mental sharpness and with the oracle's function of illuminating what is obscure.

kw-guidance.name: Guidance
kw-guidance.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with Guidance in the Etteilla system — the direction provided by the oracle, by authority figures, or by inner wisdom. Guidance in the Etteilla tradition is associated with the High Priest and other figures of spiritual and social authority, as well as with the oracle itself as a tool for navigating uncertain situations.

kw-harmony.name: Harmony
kw-harmony.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with Harmony in the Etteilla system — the quality of agreement, peace, and the concordance of disparate elements into a unified whole. Harmony in the Etteilla tradition is associated with the stable mid-range pip cards and with positive resolutions in the reading.

kw-intuition.name: Intuition
kw-intuition.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with Intuition in the Etteilla system — the direct knowing that bypasses conscious reasoning, the inner voice or felt sense of what is true. Intuition in the Etteilla tradition is associated with the Cups suit's emotional intelligence and with the oracle reading itself as an act of non-rational perception.

kw-manifestation.name: Manifestation
kw-manifestation.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with Manifestation in the Etteilla system — the process by which inner intentions become outer realities. Manifestation in the Etteilla tradition is associated with the early Genesis cards' depiction of creation and with the Coin suit's domain of practical material results.

kw-nurturing.name: Nurturing
kw-nurturing.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with Nurturing in the Etteilla system — the quality of caring support, the tending of what is growing or vulnerable. Nurturing in the Etteilla tradition is associated with the Queen figures across the suits and with the Cups suit's emotional care.

kw-planning.name: Planning
kw-planning.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with Planning in the Etteilla system — the capacity for forethought, preparation, and the systematic organization of resources toward a goal. Planning in the Etteilla tradition is associated with the Prudence trump and with the methodical Coin suit's patient accumulation.

kw-skill.name: Skill
kw-skill.Scene: A keyword axis grouping items associated with Skill in the Etteilla system — the developed competence in a particular domain, the mastery acquired through practice. Skill in the Etteilla tradition is associated with the Magician trump and with the craftsman-related pip cards in the Coin and Wands suits.

axis-keyword.name: By Keyword
axis-keyword.Scene: A navigational axis organizing all items in the Etteilla deck by keyword — grouping the cards by their associated divinatory themes and qualities. The keyword axis allows navigation across the deck through themes like balance, creativity, wisdom, and manifestation rather than through suit or trump sequence.
